Money you spent. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give back, to get back', paired with 'возвращать'.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come in, to enter', paired with 'входить'.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.

meanings.note: Wild canine mammal. Common masculine noun meaning 'wolf' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The kind wolf is looking for the bunny.

examples.text: В сказке серый волк говорил голосом человека.
examples.trans: In the fairy tale the grey wolf spoke with a human voice.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to prepare, get ready', paired with 'приготовиться'.

examples.trans: We are simply preparing for the morning show.
The students were preparing for the exam.
And little Grisha is preparing for the morning show.

давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.

meanings.note: About people. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind; good').
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!

meanings.note: comparative adverb used as imperative spur

examples.trans: Come on, come on, faster, guys!

meanings.note: Diminutive of заяц. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'йчик'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'little bunny' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Look for the little bunny, Grisha!
A little bunny sat under the bush.
The kind wolf is looking for the bunny.

записать.gloss: to write down; to save (a contact)

meanings.note: Записан как... = saved as. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to write down; to save (a contact)', paired with 'записывать'.

Записан как... = saved as. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to write down; to save (a contact)', paired with 'записывать'.

examples.text: Я знаю, как я у тебя записан.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hello'.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Imperative: извини / извините. Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.en: to look around, look about oneself

examples.trans: Have a look around if you wish.

examples.text: Он вошёл в комнату и осмотрелся.
examples.trans: He entered the room and looked around.

meanings.en: to drive away, move vehicle elsewhere
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'огнать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drive away, move away', paired with 'отгонять'.

examples.trans: I will move the van away for now.
The driver moved the car to the garage.

проходить.gloss: to go through; to come in

meanings.note: 'Проходите!' = Come in! (inviting a guest)

Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go through; to come in', paired with 'пройти'.

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Vika, Pasha! I'm so glad. Come in, please.

meanings.note: + genitive plural: пять рублей. Core Russian num meaning 'five' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.
examples.trans: But we're only just starting. In a month there'll be five thousand.

meanings.note: informal: a group of young men; ребята! = guys!

meanings.note: + на: успеть на поезд = catch the train

examples.trans: We'll make it! The president always talks for a long time.

meanings.en: morning show, school matinee, festive gathering

examples.trans: We are simply preparing for the morning show.

examples.text: Дети надели костюмы на новогодний утренник.
